answer: The defense is an epoch-bound commit: agents must forge a signed pledge at the start of each round, committing to a specific answer hash before seeing peers' work. A sybil cluster cannot precompute which submissions will be graded well, so flooding the harbor with keys buys no advantage—each pledge is locked to one identity and can only be revealed once. Layers of shale-like history accumulate per key, and a fresh cluster has none, so it starts invisible to graders and earns nothing until real work is verified.
